clue.text: Cringe maybe as a cricketing failure

definitions.meaning: to dodge or bob down in fear is one way of cringing
in cricket, a batter out without scoring makes nought, called by the waterfowl's name

explanation.surface: A batsman's embarrassing zero makes him wince with shame.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: bobbing down to avoid a blow, and a score of zero in cricket.

clue.text: Menial worker torments organisation

parts.note: to dog someone is to pursue or torment them
a body is an organisation, as in a governing body

explanation.surface: A lowly employee harasses the company.
explanation.definitionFit: A drudge who does the menial chores for others; a British informal word.

clue.text: Manage to include everybody and one could be an inspiration for poets

indicators.note: to include something is to hold it within, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: to cope is to manage
all means everybody
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone who manages to involve everyone might inspire a poet.
explanation.definitionFit: The Muse of epic poetry in Greek myth, one of the nine goddesses who inspired artists.

clue.text: Disorderly males in bus that cannot be overlooked

indicators.note: something disorderly is in a mess, so these letters are jumbled into a new order

explanation.surface: Rowdy men on a bus make a scene nobody could fail to notice.
explanation.definitionFit: Something not to be missed is something that cannot be overlooked: a direct synonym.

clue.text: Uproar is interrupting one terribly

indicators.note: something interrupting another breaks into it, so it sits inside
terribly suggests the word is badly arranged, so its letters are shuffled

explanation.surface: A din breaks in on someone dreadfully.
explanation.definitionFit: A loud racket or din is an uproar, a close synonym.

clue.text: Belonging to firm, idiot in journey is hiding identity

parts.note: in can mean belonging to, as in a member in a club
Co is the abbreviation for company, a firm

indicators.note: in places one piece inside another

parts.note: a go can be a turn or journey, as in to have a go
a nit is a fool or idiot

explanation.surface: A company fool on a trip travels under a false name.
explanation.definitionFit: Travelling under disguise with one's real self concealed means keeping one's identity hidden.

clue.text: Excluding from building in street, home with disease

indicators.note: in places the run of pieces inside the street abbreviation

parts.note: a hut is a small building
to be in is to be at home
gout is a disease of the joints

explanation.surface: Someone in a street shack at home with an illness is kept apart.
explanation.definitionFit: Barring or keeping someone out is excluding them, the same verb form.

clue.text: Cigarette end on bit of the mattress?

parts.note: a butt is the stub of a smoked cigarette

explanation.surface: A smoker drops a cigarette stub on the bed.
explanation.definitionFit: Mattresses are tufted with small fabric discs; the question mark admits this is an example.

clue.text: Posting the first bit out and the last

indicators.note: the first bit out means the opening letter is dropped

parts.note: sending a letter is posting it

explanation.surface: Mailing the first part and then the final part.
explanation.definitionFit: The final part of a story or event is its conclusion, the last of it.

clue.text: Good antique? It's very valuable

parts.note: an antique is old

explanation.surface: A good old piece is worth a great deal.
explanation.definitionFit: The precious yellow metal is the byword for something of great worth.

clue.text: Like relatively cheaper goods not considered

definitions.meaning: reduced in price, as sale goods are
dismissed or disregarded, as an idea rejected out of hand

explanation.surface: Bargain goods are overlooked by shoppers.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: marked down in price, and set aside as unworthy of attention.

clue.text: Equipment carried by wicked English group

indicators.note: a thing carried by another sits within it, so one word goes inside the other

parts.note: wicked means bad
a rig is a set of equipment, as on an oil platform

explanation.surface: A gang of villainous Englishmen lugs gear around.
explanation.definitionFit: An army unit of several battalions, and loosely any organised group such as a fire crew.

clue.text: Succeed for the first time, having cried desperately for so long

indicators.note: for the first time puts this piece at the front of the answer

parts.note: to arrive is to succeed or make it

indicators.note: done desperately suggests frantic disorder, so the letters are mixed

explanation.surface: Someone finally makes it after weeping in desperation for ages.
explanation.walkthrough: 'so long' looks like a measure of time but is a farewell. 'desperately' turns CRIED into DERCI.
explanation.definitionFit: The Italian farewell meaning goodbye, the same as the casual English parting phrase.

clue.text: Descended from mountain maybe and became depressed

definitions.meaning: made one's way off a height, as a climber does
grew low in spirits, as bad news can make one

explanation.surface: A climber came off the peak and sank into gloom.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: climbed down physically, and was brought low emotionally, an idiom for dejection.

clue.text: What's patriot done wrong to become exile?

indicators.note: something done wrong is muddled up, so these letters are put in a different order

explanation.surface: What crime has a loyal citizen committed to deserve banishment?
explanation.definitionFit: Expelling someone from a country is sending them into banishment, the noun sense of the definition.

clue.text: One wild young fellow easily made money

parts.note: a means one
fast can mean wild or dissipated in behaviour
a buck is a dashing young man

explanation.surface: A reckless youth comes into money without effort.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for profit made quickly and with little effort, often dubiously.

clue.text: Work set up on benches, drinks being provided

indicators.note: in a down clue set up means read from bottom to top, so the word runs backwards

parts.note: op is short for opus, a work
tables, like workbenches, are flat raised surfaces

explanation.surface: Work is laid out on benches while drinks are handed round.
explanation.definitionFit: Things fit to drink, as a plural noun, are drinks or beverages.

clue.text: Perish, taking a route south of col

indicators.note: in a down clue south of places the next pieces below the first

parts.note: a col is a mountain pass
a way is a route

explanation.surface: A climber dies on the path below a mountain saddle.
explanation.definitionFit: A euphemism for dying, so it means to perish.

clue.text: Pilgrim's passage, very short, a road so fouled up with oil

parts.note: V is the short form of very, as in v. good

indicators.note: something fouled up is messed up, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A short road gets messed up by an oil spill on a pilgrim's route.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fouled up' rearranges A ROAD SO plus OIL into IADOLOROSA.
explanation.definitionFit: The Jerusalem street Christ is believed to have walked to the crucifixion, followed by pilgrims.

clue.text: Possibility of non-parents taking caring role with a daughter not wanted

indicators.note: not wanted says these letters are dropped from the word

parts.note: adoption is when people not the birth parents take on raising a child
a plus D, the abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: Adoption is a possibility for a couple who would rather not have a daughter.
explanation.definitionFit: A choice open to someone is a possibility available to them, a synonym.

clue.text: A sort of hollow — pram is awkward going over it

indicators.note: in a down clue going over places the first piece above the second
something awkward is clumsily placed, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A clumsy pram keeps tipping over into a dip.
explanation.definitionFit: The hollow under the arm where it joins the shoulder is one kind of hollow.

clue.text: Gem fairy's presented to Dorothy

parts.note: a peri is a fairy or sprite in Persian mythology
Dot is a pet form of the name Dorothy

explanation.surface: A fairy hands a jewel to a girl named Dorothy.
explanation.definitionFit: A green semi-precious stone, a variety of olivine, is one kind of gem.

clue.text: Sword inflicted wound on girl

parts.note: to cut is to inflict a wound with a blade
a lass is a girl

explanation.surface: A blade wounded a young woman.
explanation.definitionFit: A short curved blade favoured by sailors and pirates is a type of sword.

clue.text: Cold meat must be hygienic

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps
lean is meat without fat

explanation.surface: Chilled meat must be kept sanitary.
explanation.definitionFit: Free from dirt and germs is the everyday sense of hygienic.

clue.text: Appealed to umpire — not out! — start of debate thereafter

indicators.note: thereafter places the next piece after the jumble
out here means put out of order, so these letters are scrambled
the start of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A cricketer appeals to the umpire, who says not out, and an argument follows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' looks like part of the umpire's ruling but signals the anagram of UMPIRE and NOT, giving IMPORTUNE.
explanation.definitionFit: To pester someone with insistent requests is to appeal to them urgently, a synonym.

clue.text: From what we hear, disease was airborne

indicators.note: what we hear signals a word that sounds like another

parts.note: flu is a disease, short for influenza

explanation.surface: Apparently the illness spread through the air.
explanation.definitionFit: Travelling through the air on wings is being airborne, the past tense of fly.

clue.text: Over-scrupulous activity of school nurse?

definitions.meaning: a school nurse checking pupils for head lice removes their eggs from hair

explanation.surface: The school nurse is fussy about her work.
explanation.walkthrough: The British school 'nit nurse' once checked pupils' hair for lice eggs.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: pedantic fault-finding, and literally picking lice eggs out of hair.

clue.text: Children's game is quiet before end of party

parts.note: P is piano, the musical direction for quiet

indicators.note: the end of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: At a party's close, children play a gentle game.
explanation.definitionFit: A guessing game where one player names something seen by its first letter, played by children.
